name: base_transform
expr: RotY(behavior.eye_angle_y) x RotX(pitch) x RotY(yaw_offset) x AC root
evidence: Controller slot 8 (360 0x8285e830), row vectors: R = rotation about Y by EyeAngleY (+0x14) x pi/180 (0x8371c0e8); N = AC slot 0x64 (0x828b2850: AC+0xbc's slot 0xc4); L = N's slot 0x28, inverted; A = AC slot 0x5c (0x828b8810: AC+0xbc's slot 0x98); G = N's world matrix (0x829909f8: N+0x80's +0x10 if set, else N+0x10). Products A x inverse(L), x G, R x that, written out by 0x8237f358. So it is N's world matrix with N's own local L swapped for A. An earlier runtime memory capture, paused at entry with the default camera: N = chr+4, where chr = AC+0xbc and chr slot 0xc4 is `lwz r3,4(r3)`. N+0x10 is a TRS record (translation, quaternion, scale), not a matrix: (-324.65, 28.2451, 649.5), (0, 0.7071, 0, 0.7071) pure yaw, scale 1. N's slot 0x28 returns N+0x10, so L = TRS(N), and G (N+0x80's +0x10) holds the same values, so inverse(L) x G = identity. Its y is the lowest of the AC's position copies; the others sit 4.06 / 7.5 / 25 m higher (waist and bounds). The camera's own matrix in that capture shows the placed point is the waist copy instead (see look_at_height); which factor carries the waist offset (likely M) is unread. A = AC slot 0x5c = M x TRS(N), where M = an AC+0x234 slot = rotation about X by AC+0x234 +0x5c and rotation about Y by +0x4. EyeAngleY is 0 on row 0; yaw offset +0x4 is 0 for the player. So base = RotX(pitch) x AC root (column vectors in the runtime). Xenia re-check pending (docs/status.md)

name: pitch
expr: each 60 Hz tick: vel = vel x (1 - 0.4) + look x 0.007; angle += vel; clamp to +-1.2217305 and zero vel when clamped. look is command float 8 in [-1, 1], positive looks up. Angle holds when the stick is released
evidence: AC+0x234 component update (360 address pending), called from the AC update 0x828bef18. Command buffer floats live at buf+0x30+4i. Index 9 (buf+0x54) is a target angle: default 2 pi, written by the AI/script path (a vtable slot 0xc8 setter), which never fires for the player. When index 9 is the sentinel, index 8 (buf+0x50) is integrated: acc = look x (block+0x18 x block+0x44) = look x 0.007, then a damped step with k = block+0x48 = 0.4 and the quadratic term 0, so each tick vel = 0.6 x vel + 0.007 x look. Caller then angle += vel x dt x 60 and clamps to block+0x50 / +0x4c = +-1.2217305 rad (+-70 deg), zeroing vel at the stop. The setter (slot 0x20) clamps look to [-1, 1]. An earlier runtime capture looking at the sky read +0x5c = 0.5489 rad (31 deg), velocity ~0. Not applied: the target-angle path (index 9), invert-Y option, the 10 deg step at block+0x54 used when state is 1. 360 addresses and a Xenia re-check pending (docs/status.md)

name: follow_rate_blend
expr: each rate: when its target changes, from = current, t = 0; t = min(t + dt, CamFollowRateInterpolateFrame / 60); rate = from + (target - from) x t / duration; all rates start at 0
evidence: Interpolator 360 0x82c1b428 (r3 = {from, value, to, target, t, duration} at +0x0..+0x14, f1 = target, f2 = frames, f3 = frame time; 14 callers in the camera code): it multiplies frames by 1/60 (0x82004408), restarts from the current value when the target differs, clamps t to the duration and lerps; with duration 0 it jumps. The per-frame update eases the look-at rates at camera +0xc0/+0xd8/+0xf0/+0x108 and the eye rates at +0x124/+0x13c/+0x154/+0x16c, then copies each +4 value to the camera rates +0x2c..+0x48. The interpolators start zeroed and nothing seeds them, so on the first update each rate climbs from 0 over 0.5 s (row 0: 30 frames). The runtime resets them when piloting starts. The 360 init of the six words is not traced

name: follow_ease
expr: each frame: target slides from last frame's target in dt x 60 steps; per step, gap = target - shown in the AC's local axes, shown += rate x gap per axis (x, y, front when local z < 0 else back); partial step uses 1 - (1 - rate)^t; first frame snaps; each step also moves shown by shake x t along local x / y
evidence: Traced with a breakpoint run on the AC block getter (360 AC slot 0xd0), which caught one caller: message 0x44 sent by the camera-effects update CamFx_update 0x82bfb748, frame time in f1. Its state 0 (CamFx_stateFollow 0x82bfb238, from the state table at 0x8371e068) adds a shake offset and a lerped y offset to the block's eye / look-at, then calls CamFx_ease 0x82bf9148(this, block, dt): the first time (this+0x60 = 0) it copies eye / look-at to this+0x20 / +0x30 and the targets to +0x40 / +0x50; after that it runs CamFx_easeStep 0x82bfbb68 for the eye (block+0, last target this+0x40, shown this+0x20, rates block+0x20..+0x2c) and for the look-at (block+0x10, this+0x50, this+0x30, rates +0x30..+0x3c), then stores the targets. The step: frames = dt x 60, step = (target - last) / frames; floor(frames) whole steps then one partial (pow 0x83271028). Each step maps the gap into the frame of the entity's vtable slot 0x88 matrix (renormalised and inverted), scales x by rate[0], y by rate[1], z by rate[2] if z < 0 else rate[3], adds the side offset this+0xb4 / +0xb8 when this+0x278 is set, and maps back. The view comes from this+0x20 / +0x30. The side offset this+0xb4 / +0xb8 is the camera shake (see shake; this+0x278 is set at init); the rate scaling at this+0x11c is delay_follow. The runtime's frame is the AC root rotation. Xenia re-check pending (docs/status.md)

evidence: 360 CamCtrl_placeEye 0x8285fe18: eye -= row x 0x8285dfe8(blender) x input[1], input[1] = offset row +0x14 EyeOffsetXOffsetRate. 0x8285dfe8 = blender+0x78 x eased(+0x44) of 0x8285d858 = controller slot 0x28 (0x8285d430: controller +0x3c, taken as 1) x action +0x40 EyeOffsetX. blender+0x74 is an interpolator (value +0x78) that 0x8285dd78 steps toward +0xc4 over action +0x5c TurnOffsetMoveFrame (0x83713b68 = 120 without an action); when action +0x5e bTrunMoveEnable is set, +0xc4 = +1 or -1 by the sign of clamp(-(controller slot 0x1c = controller +0x18), -1, 1) when nonzero (0x8285d9f0, 0x82419df0 / 0x828607f0). The blender ctor 0x8285e630 sets +0xc4 and both interpolators to 1. Runtime capture (see look_at_height): eye 6.0 m off the root along the AC's side at spawn. User check in an emulator run: the AC shows left of centre after spawn and moves to the other side when turning left. Controller +0x18 is taken as the turn input (its writer is unread); the +0x8c turn weight (eased to 1) is left out since TurnCenterDist = EyeDistance and TurnHeight = EyeHeight = 0 in every row the runtime selects (not in 24 / 49 / 90 / 190)

name: eye_place
expr: F.y >= 0: H.xz = F.xz + (normalize(F.x, 0, F.z) - F).xz x (1 - EyeApproachRate), H.y = EyeDownRate x F.y, eye = P - dist x H, look_at = eye + dist x F; else see eye_forward_shift
evidence: 0x8285fba0 picks a branch on the base transform's forward F = -row2: F.y >= 0 (level or looking up, 見上げ) -> 0x8285f928, else 0x8285f990. 0x8285f928: eye = P - dist x H (0x8285f080) with H.xz = F.xz + (normalize(F.x, 0, F.z) - F).xz x (1 - EyeApproachRate) and H.y = EyeDownRate x F.y; look-at = eye + dist x F (0x82860a20), which is P when level. P is the base point after look_at_height / look_at_offset_x. The rates come from the offset row (+0x1c / +0x20) when there is one, else behavior +0x94 / +0x98 (getters 0x8285d580 / 0x8285d5a0). Offset row 0: approach 0.3, down 1. Applied now that pitch can raise F.y

name: eye_forward_shift
expr: d = normalize(F.x, 0, F.z) x (-asin(F.y) / (pi/2)); eye = P - F x dist + EyeForwardLength x d; look_at = P + AtForwardLength x d
evidence: 0x8285f990 (looking-down branch of 0x8285fba0, 見下し). d is 0x8285f420: asinf(-F.y) / (deg2rad 0x8371c0e8 x 90 0x820146d0) times the flattened F. Row 0 EyeForwardLength is 0, AtForwardLength is 2

name: speed_blur
expr: each 1/30 s game frame (once per CamFx_update): h = ramp(|v.xz| x 216, BlurStartSpeed, BlurMaxSpeed), vt = ramp(|v.y| x 216, BlurStartSpeedV, BlurMaxSpeedV) with ramp(s, a, b) = (s - a) / (b - a) when s > a and a < b else 0; i += (clamp(h + vt, 0, 1) x action.BlurRate - i) x BlurIntpRate, clamp i to 0..1; filter alpha = clamp(trunc(BlurAlpha x i), 0, 255), offset = BlurOffset x i, thin = BlurThinPow x i, no-effect size = (BlurNoEffectSizeX, BlurNoEffectSizeY)
evidence: CamCtrl_update 360 0x82860100 copies the camera action row's BlurRate (+0x50, 0 without a row) to camera+0x58 = block+0x4c. CamFx_update 0x82bfb748 calls 0x82bfa9f0(this+0x98, f1 = block+0x4c, r6 = entity, r7 = behavior row; f2 = block+0x50 is overwritten unused). 0x82bf9c98 takes entity+0x130 (m/tick) x 216 (0x82090f20) against behavior +0xc0 / +0xc4 (horizontal) and +0xc8 / +0xcc (vertical; |v.y|), sums the two ramps (each unclamped) and clamps to 0..1. 0x82bfa9f0: this+0xa0 += (ramp x BlurRate - this+0xa0) x +0xbc BlurIntpRate, per call and not scaled by dt, then clamped to 0..1; writes byte +0 = clamp(fctiwz(+0xd4 BlurAlpha x i), 0, 255), +4 = +0xd0 BlurOffset x i, +0xc = +0x124 BlurThinPow x i, +0x10 / +0x14 = +0x128 / +0x12c no-effect size. 0x82bf9028 (from 0x827dcba0 after CamFx_update) -> 0x82bf8c20 copies it to the filter block 0x83a8b1e0 + 0x660: +0xc offset, +0x10 alpha, +0x14 1.0, +0x18 thin, +0x1c / +0x20 no-effect, +0x24..+0x2c 0 (centre), +0x30 1.0, +0x34 = i > 0, +0x38 = 1; at i = 0 alpha 0, thin 1, no-effect (0.7, 0.5). Row 0: rate 0.15, 80 / 300 km/h both ways, offset 5.16, alpha 255, thin 0.77, no-effect 0.8 x 0.6. BlurRate: stop / walk / turn / landing 0, flight / boost 4, quick boost 9, hover 6. BlurCenterThin (+0xd8, -1 on row 0) is not read on this path. Rate (Xenia probe private/xenia/blur_rate.txt, 82 s of play): 0x82bfa9f0 runs exactly once per CamFx_update 0x82bfb748 on the same thread, and CamFx_update gets f1 = 1/30 s every frame, so the ease steps 30 times a second (the runtime still steps per 60 Hz tick). Probed BlurRate (f1 at 0x82bfa9f0): 0 still / walking, 4 boosting, and 2 for about 0.8 s of a run that included firing; no state above has rate 2. this+0xbc read 0 every call, so BlurIntpRate 0.15 is read from the behavior row, not this

name: speed_blur_draw
expr: pixels inside the centre rectangle |ndc| <= no-effect size are copied; elsewhere ramp = max((|x| - nx) / (1 - nx), (|y| - ny) / (1 - ny)), w = saturate(thin x ramp x |ndc|), colour = mix(c0, mean of the 10 taps uv - k x ndc x (offset / 1280) x w for k = 0..9, alpha / 255)
evidence: Filter manager 360 0x82bbb328 lists m_ZoomBlur as its 7th filter. Its draw 360 0x82c98368 (shader ids relative to the first pixel shader, table 0x8371e978 entry 0x0c): skips when trunc(alpha x +0x54) <= 9; +0x34 = 0 projects a world centre (+0x24), else takes +0x24 / +0x28 as the NDC centre, clamped to +-(+0x4c, +0x50). With +0x38 = 0 one full-screen ZoomBlur_ZoomBlurPS (0x50); with +0x38 set (the camera path) ZoomBlur_ZoomBlurNoPS (0x52) over the centre rectangle (uv origin ((1 - nx) / 2, (1 - ny) / 2), size nx x ny), then ZoomBlur_ZoomBlurHiPS (0x51) over four frame quads (16 vertices, stride 0x20) whose outer corners carry z = +0x18 thin and inner corners 0, so z is linear from the rectangle edge to the screen edge in each quad. Constants (0x82c97ff8): c28 = (+0xc / source width, +0x14, alpha / 255, 0); alpha < 255 also sets blend factor alpha. PS3 shader/filter_shader.bnd entries 156-158 (RSX fragment programs, private/tmp/rsxfp.py): NoPS = tex0 at TEX0; HiPS: d = TEX1.xy, w = saturate(TEX1.z x |d|), taps TEX0 - k x d x U1.x x w for k = 0..9, x 0.1, then mix with the centre tap by U0.z; ZoomBlurPS: 5 taps x 0.2 with w = saturate(|d| x (1 - U2.y) + U1.y). TEX1 is assumed to be the vertex NDC (the vertex program is not decoded), sampled toward the centre, and the source width is taken as 1280
